summary: The United Arab Emirates gives many Western and East Asian passport holders a free 30-day visa on arrival, lets EU citizens stay visa-free for 90 days in any 180, and routes everyone else through pre-arranged tourist eVisas sponsored by airlines, hotels or UAE residents.

vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travelers aged nine months and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, including those who spent more than 12 hours in transit through such a country's airport.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not checked at the border for visa-on-arrival and visa-exempt visitors, though sponsored tourist visas often bundle basic cover. Private healthcare is excellent but expensive — medical insurance is strongly recommended.

onwardTicket.text: Airlines and immigration officers may require proof of an onward or return ticket, plus confirmed accommodation, especially for visa-on-arrival travelers.

notes: Duty-free allowance includes 4 liters of alcohol (non-Muslim adults) and 400 cigarettes per adult.
Many common medications (codeine, tramadol, some sleeping pills, CBD products) are controlled substances in the UAE. Carry a prescription and check whether prior approval is needed before traveling.
Narcotics offenses carry severe penalties; even trace amounts can lead to prosecution.

payments.text: Cards and contactless payments (including Apple Pay and Google Pay) are accepted almost everywhere, from malls to taxis. Cash is only occasionally useful for small shops, souks and tips.

safety.text: The UAE has very low crime and is among the safest destinations for travelers. The main risks are legal, not criminal: strict laws on drugs, medications, public behavior and online speech. Regional tensions occasionally disrupt air travel — monitor the news around departure.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — United Arab Emirates Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to March brings warm, sunny days without the extreme summer heat — the ideal season for beaches, desert trips and city sightseeing.

idp.text: United Arab Emirates is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 (UNTS vol. 125, p. 3); Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: United Arab Emirates is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for United Arab Emirates yet.

tips.text: Check your medications before flying: codeine, tramadol, strong painkillers and CBD products are controlled in the UAE. Carry the original prescription and apply for prior approval where required — arriving with unapproved controlled medicines can mean arrest.
During Ramadan, be discreet about eating, drinking and smoking in public during daylight hours out of respect; many restaurants screen off dining areas, and hours for shops and attractions change.

Drink only in licensed venues, never drink and drive (zero tolerance), and avoid offensive gestures, swearing or heated public arguments — public decency and cybercrime laws are enforced, including for social media posts.
Tap water is desalinated and technically safe to drink, though most residents prefer bottled or filtered water for taste — either is fine for brushing teeth and cooking.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the UAE?
faq.answer: No advance visa is needed. US passport holders receive a free 30-day visa on arrival at any UAE entry point, which can be extended once for a further 30 days from inside the country for a fee.

faq.question: How long can EU citizens stay in the UAE?
faq.answer: Citizens of EU countries such as Germany, France, Spain and Italy (plus Switzerland) can stay visa-free for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. No visa on arrival stamp fee, no pre-arranged visa.

faq.question: Can Indian citizens get a UAE visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Only if they hold a valid US visa, US green card, or UK/EU residence permit — that group can buy a 14-day visa on arrival, extendable once. All other Indian passport holders need a pre-arranged tourist eVisa (30 or 60 days), usually sponsored by an airline such as Emirates or Etihad, a hotel, or a UAE resident.

faq.question: How much does a UAE tourist eVisa cost?
faq.answer: Roughly 300 AED for a single-entry 30-day tourist eVisa and around 500 AED for 60 days, though the exact price varies by sponsor (airline, hotel or travel agency) and emirate. Multiple-entry versions cost more, and extensions of about 30 days are available in-country for an additional fee.

faq.question: Do I need a visa to transit through Dubai or Abu Dhabi?
faq.answer: Staying airside, no visa is needed. To leave the airport, nationalities without visa-free or visa-on-arrival access can get a transit permit through their airline: 48 hours free, or 96 hours for about 50 AED. Both must be arranged before travel.
